lines.t: No eye has seen it.
No ear has heard.
No dream could hold it.
Still, it’s written in the Word.
For those who love the Lord,
There’s more than dreams can hold.
Ask, ask—let the prayer rise.
The Lord already knows.
More, more—more than eyes have seen,
More, more—more than hearts could dream.
Before the call, He answers; while the words still rise,
The Lord hears every prayer before the last word leaves.
Flow, flow—let the fountain flow.
How far can His restoring love go?
Past the stars to the paws by the door—
More, more—there’s more in store.
More than—more than—more than dreams.
No eye, no ear, no heart could dream.
Flow, flow—overflow.
How far can His love go?
Read that line, let it breathe, run it back:
No eye caught a flash, no ear caught a track.
Dreams run wild, still they can’t touch the edge
Of all that He’s prepared for the hearts that love Him.
Ask with the whole heart, not just the right words.
Even a whisper in the dark gets heard.
First word forming, breath still in the chest—
He’s heard the prayer before the tongue says the rest.
No spotlight needed, no perfect take,
No polished speech when the voice starts to shake.
Before that call ever breaks through the night,
The Lord has an answer—the promise holds tight.
No eye could see it.
No ear could hear it.
No dream could hold it.
Still, the heart can ask.
More.
More, more—more than eyes have seen,
More, more—more than hearts could dream.
Before the call, He answers; while the words still rise,
The Lord hears every prayer before the last word leaves.
Flow, flow—let the fountain flow.
How far can His restoring love go?
Past the stars to the paws by the door—
More, more—there’s more in store.
Little paws used to tap down the hallway,
One small sound could turn around a hard day.
Collar on a hook, quiet by the chair—
Love leaves a trace when a friend isn’t there.
And the fountain doesn’t stop at the edge of that ache,
Doesn’t pass by a bond that the world calls small.
The Lord who holds the stars knows those pawprints too—
Even the smallest lives aren’t small to Him at all.
Let the prayer rise for the ones held dear,
For the soft little heartbeat that once slept near.
How far does that fountain of love overflow?
Past the last goodbye, farther than dreams can go.
From the farthest star
To a pawprint in the dust,
There’s no corner of creation
Too small for His love.
All things, all things—
Restored by the Lord.
Even those beloved paws
Are held in that hope.
Before the call—
He answers.
While the words still rise—
He hears.
How far does the fountain flow?
Farther than dreams.
More, more—more than eyes have seen,
More, more—more than hearts could dream.
Before the call, He answers; while the words still rise,
The Lord hears every prayer before the last word leaves.
Flow, flow—let the fountain flow.
How far can His restoring love go?
Past the stars to the paws by the door—
More, more—there’s more in store.
No eye has seen it.
No dream could hold it.
From the farthest star
To the smallest paw.
